title: Governance pillar — video 03 talking-point and screen rubric
note: Scored by gen-ceo-video-review.js --pillar governance. `judge_on: auto` criteria are measured by the deterministic probes in generators/lib/rubric-review.js and must not be supplied as verdicts. `screen` criteria are judged on the panels the deck embeds and need a `ref` (story#scN:panel.png). Evidence quoted only from an `also` story caps a narration verdict at partial. Keep ids stable: past verdicts bind to them.

scale.covered: Stated explicitly and clearly enough that a first-time viewer would take the point away.
scale.partial: Touched, implied, or named without enough substance to land — a viewer could miss it.
scale.missed: Not present in the narration at all.

weights.must: The video fails its job without this.
weights.should: Expected; its absence is a real gap worth fixing before the next cut.
weights.nice: Strengthens the story; acceptable to trade away for time.

dimensions.name: Governance — products people can find, trust and fix
dimensions.framing: Landed data becomes governed data products with owners, scores the platform computes, lineage it resolves and a stewardship loop that closes. The viewer should see each of those on the live tenant and know who is accountable.

criteria.name: Every scene shows a real tenant capture
criteria.expect: Each scene of the Governance video embeds a qlik_panels/*.png captured from the live tenant. No drawn chart, no missing file, and no panel edited after capture — the relabelled dp_lineage.png scores partial at best.
criteria.source: plan § E Probes; § Context 4 (dp_lineage.png has an OLH label painted on after capture)

criteria.name: The panels show governance on the live tenant
criteria.expect: The data product, profiling, trust score, lineage, stewardship and glossary scenes each show that object on the live tenant, and the panel agrees with the narration: the trust score spoken is the one on screen, lineage is resolved by the platform rather than painted, the sprint shown is the one described.

criteria.name: A data product with an owner, schema, SLA and trust target
criteria.expect: At least one data product is described with a named owner, a schema, a refresh SLA and a trust-score target: Supply Chain Health — Henrik Jansen, target 0.85; Last Mile Performance — Sophie Müller.

criteria.name: The trust score is computed, not asserted
criteria.expect: The trust score is computed by the platform from validity, completeness, discoverability and usage and recalculated as the data changes — not a figure someone typed into a wiki or a dashboard.

criteria.name: Profiling turns the nightmares into row counts
criteria.expect: Profiling output is spoken as counts tied to the nightmares: products with no weight on file, addresses that cannot be resolved, perishable positions with no lot number.

criteria.name: The stewardship loop closes
criteria.expect: Records automation cannot fix land in a stewardship sprint, a human steward corrects them, and the correction flows back into the pipeline: detect, notify, review, correct, validate, with the human at the judgement step.

criteria.name: A Data Quality Agent writes the rule
criteria.expect: A Data Quality Agent turns a business rule — 'every perishable item must have a lot number' — into a quality rule and shows the violations.

criteria.name: Lineage and impact analysis
criteria.expect: Every gold field traces back through silver and bronze to the source system, and impact analysis shows which products, apps and models a source change would break.

criteria.name: A governed business glossary
criteria.expect: Business terms are governed — owned, statused and linked to the dataset that computes them — so two teams read the same number.

criteria.name: Traceability the regulator demands
criteria.expect: Lot-level traceability is tied to the regulation behind it: EC 178/2002 'one step back, one step forward' and the NVWA citation that followed the lettuce recall.

criteria.name: Shareable over an API and in the marketplace
criteria.expect: The data products are shareable over an API and discoverable in the marketplace, so the next team does not rebuild them.
